outcome: Maternal morbidity (hemorrhage, uterine infection, uterine rupture)
Neonatal morbidity (5-minute APGAR score <7, NICU admission)
cohort: 688 women with a history of a single prior cesarean delivery presenting for cervical ripening
finding: The study found no significant difference in maternal or neonatal morbidity between women who underwent cervical ripening with a Foley balloon compared to oxytocin, but the rate of vaginal delivery was lower in the Foley balloon group.
mod_finding: The study found no difference in maternal and neonatal morbidity between cervical ripening with a Foley balloon and oxytocin, but the rate of successful vaginal delivery was lower in the Foley balloon group.
